skills.bodyMd:
# Scheduled tasks

A scheduled task is something the agent agreed to do for one user later: once, or on a
repeat, at a wall-clock time in that user's zone. When it comes due, the router wakes the
agent in the user's own conversation with the task's instructions. The agent's answer is
the delivery.

How the code works, its terms and the tests behind each rule:
`acceleration/internal/scheduling/AGENTS.md`. What is decided and what is not done:
`.factory/features/scheduled-tasks.md`. Paths below are under `acceleration/`.

## One example, start to end

```
 Alice, 14:02 (Europe/Amsterdam): "remind me to call the dentist in 20 minutes"
   agent -> schedule_task {title: "Dentist", instructions: "Remind Alice to call the dentist.", in: "PT20M"}
   tool  -> {"id": "...", "schedule": "Once, Wed 21 Oct 2026 at 14:22 (Europe/Amsterdam)", "next": "..., in 20 minutes"}
 14:22  worker claims the occurrence -> run "running"
        agent is sent <scheduled_task ...>Remind Alice to call the dentist.</scheduled_task>
        agent writes "Time to call the dentist!" in Alice's conversation
        run "delivered", delivered_to "conversation"; task "completed"
```

The tool and its fields: `internal/session/schedule_tools.go:36`. The prompt the agent is
sent: `scheduledPrompt`, `internal/api/scheduled_delivery.go:456`.

## Turn it on

Scheduling is a block on the agent config (`AgentScheduling`, `internal/api/configs.go:2103`):

| Field | What it does | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `scheduling.enabled` | Offers the model the four tools: `schedule_task`, `list_scheduled_tasks`, `update_scheduled_task`, `cancel_scheduled_task` | off |
| `scheduling.max_tasks_per_user` | Active tasks one user may hold on this config, 1 to 100 | 25 (`scheduling.MaxActivePerUser`) |
| `scheduling.default_timezone` | The IANA zone a task takes when neither the call, the session nor the user names one. An unknown zone is a 400 `invalid_timezone` | none: a task with no zone is refused with `timezone_unknown` |

The tools also need (`Manager.schedulingRunner`, `internal/session/schedule_tools.go:106`):

- a router with a database;
- a session that is not incognito, opened on a config;
- a caller that is a verified user or a backend acting for one (`X-Stream-User-Id`), or the
  person who wrote in an SMS (Telnyx) or WhatsApp thread or a 1:1 iMessage (Linq) chat, and
  only when that person writes, not someone else in the thread (the task is theirs and keeps
  the thread). A Linq chat is 1:1 only while its latest message says `data.chat.is_group`
  `false`: the bridge then records the sender as the chat's person
  (`channel_threads.chat_person`). A group chat, a chat whose message does not say, a thread
  linked before that column, and a Slack thread get no tools. A guest or an anonymous caller
  gets no tools.

A task made in an SMS or WhatsApp thread or a 1:1 iMessage chat comes back in that thread:
the router opens the thread's conversation, the agent answers the task there, and the reply is
texted to the person from the line. Its run says `delivered_to` `sms`, `whatsapp` or
`imessage` once the line took the
reply; a reply the line refused is `delivery_failed`, and the retry sends the same reply,
files included, without a second turn; a thread removed while the turn ran is `thread_gone`,
final (`internal/api/scheduled_thread_delivery.go`); a Linq chat that became a group is
`thread_gone`, final, too. Such a task's `deliver_to` reads `sms`, `whatsapp` or `imessage`
and cannot be changed.

The REST create does not need `scheduling.enabled` (`internal/api/scheduled_tasks.go:752`).

A follow-up needs a kept conversation, and a conversation is kept only in Stream Chat. A
router without a usable Stream app refuses every session that is not incognito with 400
`not_configured` (`session.ErrNoStreamKeys`, `ErrStreamKeysRejected` in
`internal/session/stream_keys.go`), so it has no conversation to deliver a task into.

## Schedule one locally

1. Run the router per the repo-root `AGENTS.md` (Local dev) with `ROUTER_AUTH_MODE=proxy`
   (the Volt override sets it, `.claude/skills/dashboard/SKILL.md`). The commands below name
   the app with `X-Customer-Id`, which only `proxy` mode reads; in `api_key` mode send the
   credentials of "Schedule one on staging" instead. In `noauth` mode the router reads no `X-Stream-User-Id`
   (`internal/auth/auth.go:89`), so a create is refused ("name the user the task is for
   with X-Stream-User-Id") and no session gets the tools.
2. Make a config with scheduling on. In `proxy` mode without `proxy_declares_kind`, a request
   naming its app with `X-Customer-Id` and no `Stream-Auth-Type` is a backend
   (`internal/auth/auth.go:291`):

   ```bash
   R=http://localhost:8080
   H=(-H 'X-Customer-Id: examples' -H 'Content-Type: application/json')
   curl -s "$R/v1/agents/configs" "${H[@]}" -d '{
     "name": "reminders",
     "instructions": "You are a helpful assistant.",
     "scheduling": {"enabled": true, "default_timezone": "Europe/Amsterdam"}
   }'
   ```

   A config with that name already exists on a second run (409 `name_taken`). Use another
   name, or give the existing config the same block with `PATCH /v1/agents/configs/{id}`.
3. Schedule through the agent: open a session for a user, then write to it.

   ```bash
   U=(-H 'X-Stream-User-Id: alice')
   SID=$(curl -s "$R/v1/agents/sessions" "${H[@]}" "${U[@]}" \
     -d '{"agent": "reminders", "timezone": "Europe/Amsterdam"}' | jq -r .id)
   curl -s "$R/v1/agents/sessions/$SID/respond" "${H[@]}" "${U[@]}" \
     -d '{"text": "remind me to stretch in 20 minutes", "request_id": "remind-1"}'
   curl -s "$R/v1/agents/sessions/$SID/commands/remind-1" "${H[@]}" "${U[@]}"   # state: thinking, then completed
   ```

   A text session with a named user needs a durable command, so `respond` takes a
   `request_id` (without it: 400 `personal conversations require a command ID`,
   `internal/session/session.go:507`). `GET .../commands/{request_id}`
   (`internal/api/sessions.go:1147`) answers the command's `state` (`thinking`, then
   `completed`), not the reply text: read that in the conversation on the dashboard. The
   model has made the task when the list in step 4 shows it.

   Or through REST (`createScheduledTask`, `internal/api/scheduled_tasks.go:742`). Name the
   agent with `agent`, `config_id` or `session_id`:

   ```bash
   TASK=$(curl -s "$R/v1/agents/scheduled-tasks" "${H[@]}" "${U[@]}" -d '{
     "agent": "reminders", "title": "Stretch",
     "instructions": "Remind Alice to stretch and ask how her back is.",
     "schedule": {"at": "09:00", "repeat": "FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO,TU,WE,TH,FR"}
   }' | jq -r .id)
   ```

   `TASK` is the new task's id. A task the tool made: take its id from the list in step 4
   (with one task, `jq -r '.items[0].id'` gives it).

   Without `session_id`, the first occurrence opens a session for the user.
4. Watch it. Fire it now without moving the schedule, then read its runs:

   ```bash
   curl -s "$R/v1/agents/scheduled-tasks?state=active" "${H[@]}" "${U[@]}" | jq '.items[] | {id, title, next_run_at, last_run_at}'
   curl -s -X POST "$R/v1/agents/scheduled-tasks/$TASK/run" "${H[@]}" "${U[@]}"   # 202, the run
   curl -s "$R/v1/agents/scheduled-tasks/$TASK/runs" "${H[@]}" "${U[@]}" | jq '.items[] | {scheduled_for, trigger, state, delivered_to, error}'
   docker compose logs -f router | grep -i 'scheduled task' | grep -v 'Failed to forward'
   ```

   The `grep -v` drops the job queue's `Failed to forward scheduled tasks` noise. A delivered
   run logs nothing; its run row says `delivered`. Open the session on the
   dashboard to read the agent's message.

## Schedule one on staging

Staging is `https://accelerate-staging.gcp.stream-io-api.com`, behind Stream's proxy. The proxy
wants `api_key` and `stream-auth-type: jwt` for any token, and a server token is HS256
`{"server": true}` signed with the app's secret (`sdks/js/src/backend.ts:318`,
`signToken` at `:486`). Never print the secret or the token.

```bash
set -a; . ./.env; set +a          # STREAM_API_KEY, STREAM_API_SECRET; prints nothing
# node 22 reads the secret from its environment, so it never appears in a command line
TOKEN=$(node -e '
const c = require("node:crypto");
const b = (v) => Buffer.from(JSON.stringify(v)).toString("base64url");
const now = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000);
const input = b({ alg: "HS256", typ: "JWT" }) + "." + b({ server: true, iat: now, exp: now + 3600 });
process.stdout.write(input + "." + c.createHmac("sha256", process.env.STREAM_API_SECRET).update(input).digest("base64url"));
')
R=https://accelerate-staging.gcp.stream-io-api.com
A=(-H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'stream-auth-type: jwt' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'X-Stream-User-Id: alice')
curl -s "$R/v1/agents/scheduled-tasks?api_key=$STREAM_API_KEY" "${A[@]}" | jq '.items | length'
```

Every call from "Schedule one locally" works with `"${A[@]}"` in place of
`"${H[@]}" "${U[@]}"` and `api_key=$STREAM_API_KEY` on the URL: after `?` when the URL has no
query yet, after `&` when it has one (`...?state=active&api_key=$STREAM_API_KEY`). Staging logs: the `deploy`
skill.

## Nothing arrived?

Read the task, then its runs, then the logs, in that order.

| Check | How | What it means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Task `state` | `GET /v1/agents/scheduled-tasks/{id}` | `paused`: a pause, or its config was deleted (`internal/api/configs.go:308`). `failed`: five failed occurrences in a row (`maxConsecutiveFailures`), or a last occurrence that failed; resume clears it. A failed task with no occurrence left, or a paused one that did not sleep through its time, answers resume with 400 `schedule_in_past`: PATCH a new schedule first, 15 min out at the soonest. A paused one-shot whose time passed while paused is completed with a `missed` run (`task_paused`). `completed`: a one-shot ran, or the repeat has nothing left |
| `next_run_at`, `upcoming` | same | In the task's zone. Wrong hour: the zone (below) |
| `schedule.timezone` | same | Resolved at create from the call, the session, `users.timezone`, then `default_timezone`. A session opened with a zone moves `users.timezone` (`internal/api/session_create.go:76`) |
| `quiet_hours` | same | An occurrence due inside them is held to their end: its run stays `running` with nothing sent. A run by hand is never held |
| The runs | `GET /v1/agents/scheduled-tasks/{id}/runs` | No run at all: the occurrence was never claimed (worker logs). `running` long after `scheduled_for`: held, or a worker is on it; a run by hand whose router stopped stays `running` until the daily prune writes it `missed`, a day after it started |
| Run `state` `missed` | same | Too late: a one-shot over 24 h, a repeat over 1 h (`scheduler.go:51`), a call over 15 min (a run by hand too), or with under 11.5 min of the occurrence left. Or `error` `task_paused`: a one-shot resumed after its time, or an occurrence a move's cut-over skipped whose run the source had started |
| Run `error` | same | See the reason table below |
| Limit | create or resume answers 409 `too_many_tasks` | The user holds `max_tasks_per_user` active tasks on this config |
| Edit refused | update, pause or resume answers 409 `task_changed` | The task changed between the request's read and its save (another edit or pause, or a worker's claim, hold, finish or session write; a lease renewal is not a change): nothing was saved, so read it again and retry. The agent's `update_scheduled_task` is refused the same way |
| The tools | the model never calls `schedule_task` | `scheduling.enabled` off, incognito, a guest or anonymous caller, or a `noauth` router |
| Device PATCH refused | `PATCH /v1/agents/scheduled-tasks/{id}` answers 400 `interval_too_short` | A device moves `next` only to or past the run still pending (`scheduling.CheckLater`), and a `schedule` whose first run is earlier than a pending one. While that run is due or in flight, the `schedule` starts no earlier than the stored schedule's next occurrence after it (`owedRun`); with none after it, an active task is refused, and so is a paused one whose due run already ran (a pause over a run in flight settles it). A paused task that slept through its time, or a failed one, keeps the floor. With no run pending, `next` has nothing to move. A backend key keeps the 15 min floor (`scheduling.CheckMove`) |
| Tool refused | `schedule_task` answers `interval_too_short` or `scheduled_turn` | The agent's first run is 15 min from now at the soonest (`scheduling.MinMove`). A turn a task fired cannot schedule a task, nor reschedule, snooze or resume one; it may list, pause, skip and cancel |
| Old history gone | a completed or failed task 404, or old runs missing | A daily job deletes runs finished over 90 days ago, and completed or failed tasks over 90 days old (`ScheduledTasksKept`); active and paused tasks stay. It redacts the changes recorded of what it deletes (`ScheduledTasks.Prune`), and deleting a task redacts those of it and its runs (`ScheduledTasks.Delete`) |
| Session deleted | task 404 | Deleting a session deletes the tasks made in it or following up in it, with their runs, and redacts the changes recorded of them (`DeleteForSession`) |
| User forgotten | task 404, its runs gone | `router usage forget-user` deleted every task of that user in the app, with its runs, and redacted the changes recorded of them (`ForgetUserTasks`) |
| Team left | a device's task 404, missing from its list | In an app with `agent_teams`, a task on a config of a team the user is no longer in is not there to their device, nor one on a deleted config, except to pause or delete it; their backend still reaches it. A router holds a user's teams for 30 s, so a removal is seen within that; held teams that refuse ask Stream again first, at most once a second, and stand while it cannot be asked |

Run `error` codes (`internal/scheduling/scheduler.go:105`):

| Code | Meaning | Retried |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `delivery_failed` | Any other failure, or the occurrence was claimed three times (`maxScheduledTaskRunAttempts`: the first claim, the take-up after a hold, one after a lost worker) with no call placed; with a call placed, the cap keeps the reason that call ended under, or gives `already_called` (`capFailure`) | yes, unless it was claimed three times or a call was already placed (`scheduled_delivery.go:783`, `:857`) |
| `timed_out` | The occurrence used its 20 min (`occurrenceBudget`) | no |
| `schedule_unreadable` | The stored schedule no longer parses; the task is paused | no |
| `user_on_call` | The user stayed on a call through the 10 min window | yes |
| `channel_unreachable` | SMS, WhatsApp or iMessage would refuse: never wrote on it, opted out, outside WhatsApp's 24 h window, no line. On a thread task: opted out (before the turn or by the time the reply is sent), or the sandbox gate holds it back (a thread task's text refused for money is not this: it has the money codes below) | yes; not for a thread task's opted-out person |
| `outside_window` | A WhatsApp thread task whose person last wrote over 24 h ago, with no template to send after the window | no |
| `thread_gone` | A thread task's thread no longer exists, or is not its user's thread of its customer | no |
| `connection_removed` | A thread task's line (its connection) was removed | no |
| `not_in_team` | In an app that keeps each team's agent configs to its own users (`agent_teams`), the end user the task is for is no longer in its config's team: one they made (`caller_kind` not `server`), or one the agent made talking with them (`created_by` `agent`, outside a thread), whoever opened that chat. The agent is not run and no session is opened. A task the backend made through the API, or the agent made on an SMS, WhatsApp or iMessage thread, is not checked; teams Stream could not read fail the attempt as `delivery_failed`, retried | no |
| `no_reply` | The agent said nothing and made no file to carry | yes |
| `reply_failed` | The reply failed, or was cancelled or interrupted and, when run once more under `st_<run>_r1`, was cut off again (a text channel's or a thread task's first cut-off also gives it, and the retry runs it again) | yes |
| `no_phone_number` | The user never texted this agent by SMS; a number used only on WhatsApp is not rung | yes |
| `no_agent_number` | The config has no SMS line to ring from | yes |
| `not_answered` | Nobody picked up within the 90 s ring | no |
| `already_called` | A call was placed for this occurrence already, and its end is not recorded; no channel after `phone` is tried. That call may have carried the task out, so the run leaves the failure streak as it is and the task moves on as after a run that did not fail (a one-shot is `completed`) | no |
| `account_suspended`, `insufficient_credits`, `system_limit_reached`, `spend_limit_reached`, `user_limit_reached` | A step the organization may not pay for was refused for money (suspended, no credit left, or a spent limit): an SMS, WhatsApp or iMessage text or a thread task's reply (`dlc.ErrUnpaid`, or its reservation), the task's session opening or being carried on, a turn the model refuses, on a text channel (`captureReply`, which ends the walk over the channels, `refusedTurn`), in the conversation (`followUpInConversation` waits for the turn to end; a turn that ends any other way is still `delivered`) or on a thread task (`deliverOnThread`), or its call, placed or not: a placed call whose session cannot open fails under the refusal's code (`carryOutOnCall`); on an answered call, a turn refused before the agent answered anything hangs up (`carryOutAnswered`), the task's turn cut off by the caller included, and a refusal after that is a later turn's, still `delivered`: a refusal for money names no turn, so a call's session keeps it (`Session.UnansweredRefusal`, which `carryOutAnswered` reads) and gives it to the conversation, transcript or not, only while the agent has not answered since the task's turn was typed (`Session.refusedUnanswered`). The other steps read how the turn ended from the conversation, which keeps the error that failed the reply (`Session.FollowUpFailure`, `turnRefusal`), never from the session's events alone, which a watcher that falls behind loses; a text channel carries only its own follow-up's reply, read back once its turn ends (`readBackReply`). A turn that ended while no attempt watched it, such as one an attempt cut short left running, fails the same way while the session that ran it is still open. A refusal for money is kept on the failed reply's message in Chat (`support_money_refusal`, read back by `commandsIn`), so it survives the conversation being opened again (a restart, a drain, or the end of the session's unwatched grace): the retry ends under the same code, as before the reopen. The run records the refusal's own code (`deliveryReason`, `scheduled_delivery.go:356`), never `channel_unreachable` or `delivery_failed`, and the router warns, naming the task | no (`unpaid`, `scheduled_delivery.go:400`) |
| `spend_check_unavailable` | The router could not check what the organization has spent, so it refused the step for now (`policy.Transient`). A turn it refused runs once more on the retry, under `st_<run>_r1`: the scheduler hands the next attempt the reason this one failed under (`deliverWithRetries`) and records it on the run, so a router that takes the run over after a crash or a lost lease reruns the turn too, a hand-off to the router holding the session carries it (`scheduledHandOff.Earlier`), and `replyCommand` reruns a failed reply after a money code. A conversation rerun refused as well fails the attempt under the same code (`followUpInConversation`), so the run fails once its retries are spent. A reply that failed for any other reason is read back as it was. A placed call is rung once: refused this way, its session or its answered turn fails the run under this code, final, with the call kept on the run (`callEnded`), so the user is not rung again | yes (`unpaid` leaves it retryable) |
| `task_paused` | On a `missed` run: a one-shot whose time came while it was paused, or an occurrence the cut-over of a move skipped whose run the source had started | — |

A failure is retried after 30 s, 2 min and 10 min (`deliveryRetries`) only when the failure
is not final; with several channels, it is final only when every channel's failure is.

it also finds the job queue's `Failed to forward scheduled tasks`, which is noise):

| `a scheduled task's occurrence failed: it was started this many times and its worker was lost each time` | error | `scheduler.go:322` |
| `a scheduled task was too late to deliver` | info | `scheduler.go:351` |
| `a scheduled task changed under its run; its delivery was stopped` | info | `scheduler.go:364` |
| `a scheduled task failed to deliver` | warn | `scheduler.go:372` |
| `could not hold a scheduled task` | error | `scheduler.go:469` |

skills.name: sdk-dart
skills.desc: How to build and extend the Flutter SDK in sdks/dart. Read this before changing stream_agents (its core, chat or rtc area), the Flutter demo's use of Stream's AI components, or before adding a Dart client for a new endpoint.
skills.body:
---
name: sdk-dart
description: How to build and extend the Flutter SDK in sdks/dart. Read this before changing stream_agents (its core, chat or rtc area), the Flutter demo's use of Stream's AI components, or before adding a Dart client for a new endpoint.
---

# Dart SDK conventions

The per-language half of [sdk](../sdk/SKILL.md). It records the decisions the packages in
[`sdks/dart`](../../../sdks/dart) already follow, so a change lands consistently rather than
re-litigating them. It is a **client-side** SDK: what a phone, a browser or a desktop app does.
Folder sync, dispatch and writing configs are backend work and stay out.

Dart 3.12 and Flutter 3.44 are the floors, because Stream Chat 10.4's are; Stream Video 1.6's
are lower.

## The package

One Flutter package, `stream_agents` in `sdks/dart/stream_agents`. Inside it, three areas:

```
lib/src/core  pure Dart: generated client, socket, conversation state
lib/src/chat  pure Dart: the conversation's Stream Chat channel   -> core
lib/src/rtc   joining the call over Stream Video                  -> core
```

Each area is self-contained: `lib/src/<area>` and `test/<area>` hold all of it, and the only way
in from another area is one import. `test/area_boundaries_test.dart` enforces it:

   cannot slip in. `chat` adds `stream_chat` and `core`'s barrel to that list.
2. `chat` and `rtc` reach `core` only, never each other.
3. Across areas, only through the area's barrel (`package:stream_agents/src/core/core.dart`);
   inside one, relative imports.
4. `stream_chat` is `chat`'s alone; `stream_video_flutter` and `image` are `rtc`'s.
5. A test under `test/<area>` imports its own area (barrel or internals), the barrels its area
   reaches, or, in `rtc` only, `package:stream_agents/stream_agents.dart`. `test/core` and

type goes in its area's barrel.

  it runs on the web: `package:http` and `package:web_socket` pick the platform themselves.
- `rtc` keeps Stream Video's types out of `core`. `VoiceState.call` is the one Stream type it
  exposes, because rendering video needs it.
- **No conversation views.** The views are Stream Chat's AI components,
  `stream_chat_flutter_ai`, which the app adds itself, as the Swift SDK leaves them to
  `StreamChatAI`; see [Views](#views). There was a `ui` package with widgets of its own; it went
  the way Swift's did, so the two SDKs stay one shape.

  `core`. Import it with a prefix (`as stream`): it exports a `TokenProvider` of its own.

  `stream_chat: ^10.4.0`), as Swift's `from:` and JavaScript's `^` do: a published package
  pinned to one version would refuse every app on another patch. Raising a floor is a
  deliberate change: read the changelog, rerun the rtc tests, and check the APIs used (listed

Stream Video's singleton: use `StreamVideo.create`, never the `StreamVideo(...)` factory, which
installs a process-wide instance and collides with a host that has its own.

## Stream is set up once

The key, `userId` and token are the one identity for the router, Stream Chat and Stream Video.
`Backend` fetches the token single-flighted once and reuses it across router requests, socket
handshakes and Stream clients, refreshing only on an HTTP 401 (with a single retry) or
`streamCredentials(refresh: true)`. `Backend.shared(kind, open:, disconnect:)` holds one client
per `kind:apiKey:userId`: sessions asking at once share one opening, one that failed to open is
opened again, and `withUser` keeps the registry so another user gets their own. `Backend.give`
holds the app's own client, which `StreamAgents.disconnect()` never touches; it closes only what
`shared` built. Beside a `customerId` the key is Stream's alone and the router is reached by
customer id.

- `chat`: `agents.useChat(client)` and `session.chat()`, which answers the
  conversation's `Channel`, unwatched. A session with no conversation is a `StateError`.
- `rtc`: `agents.useVideo(client)` and `VoiceSession.join()`, which joins the
  session's `callType:callId`. Leaving disposes nothing.
- Dart has no overloading, hence `useChat` and `useVideo` rather than Kotlin's `use`. A
  client for another user, or a missing key, user or token, is an `ArgumentError`.

## State

`LiveValue<T>`: a `value` and a `stream` that emits the current value first, then each change.
`LiveValueController` skips equal values and conflates while a listener is paused. No
dependency on provider, riverpod, bloc or rxdart — a host adapts it in a line, such as a
`StreamBuilder` over `stream` with `initialData: value`, without which its first frame has no data.

The state machine is an **immutable value**, `Conversation`, with `apply(event)` returning the
next value (or `this` when nothing changed, so equality skips a rebuild). That is what makes it
testable without a network, and it is where new event handling goes.

`AgentSession.events()` hands each caller its own bounded stream (256), and finishes a listener
that falls that far behind rather than buffering without bound. Never one shared broadcast
stream property. Answering a tool call does not depend on anybody listening: it happens inside
`AgentSession`'s own read loop.

## The socket

`package:web_socket`, one read loop per connection.

- A close with 1000 (the router's "the session ended") or one we asked for finishes the stream;
  anything else throws `SocketClosedException` with the code.
- A frame that cannot be decoded is skipped, not fatal.
- Closing is idempotent and sends 1000.
- A handshake carries none of the SDK's headers, neither `X-Stream-Client` nor `User-Agent`
  (off the web, dart:io sends its own `Dart/<version>`): `package:web_socket` takes no headers,
  so a socket's credentials are all in its query.
- **No automatic reconnection.** `respond` and `tool_result` are not idempotent and the protocol
  has nothing to resume from. `AgentSession.connection` reports `Disconnected(failure)` and the
  caller decides.
- A tool result echoes `request_id` and `turn_id` only when the call carried a `request_id`; a
  bare `turn_id` routes to a path that fails for a persisted session.

Frames in tests are quoted verbatim from `frameOf` in
[`sessionws.go`](../../../acceleration/internal/api/sessionws.go).

## The generated client

`tool/generate.dart` reads the spec and writes `lib/src/core/generated/api.dart`: one model
class per schema reached by an allowlisted operation, and an `Operations` class with a method
per operation. Committed, formatted, never hand-edited, **never exported**. Every public type is
hand-written in `models.dart` and mapped in `convert.dart`, so a spec field is invisible until
it is wrapped and the SDK's semver is not the schema's.

- The allowlist (`operations`, `sockets`) fails generation if an id is missing or not marked
  `x-client-accessible`. Adding an endpoint means adding its id and rerunning.
- `--check` regenerates in memory and fails if the committed file differs. Run it in CI.
- Enums are strings in generated code and Dart enums with an `unknown` value in `models.dart`.
- Dates go through `parseRouterDate`: Go writes up to nine fractional digits, Dart reads six.
- Generated `toJson` omits nulls. **Null means omit** and let the config or the router decide,
  never a copy of the server's default.
- A wrong type in an answer throws `UnreadableException` naming the field, not a `TypeError`.

## Errors

`sealed class AgentsException implements Exception`: `RouterException` (status, message, the
operation; `isServerSideOnly` on 403), `TransportException` (no answer at all),
`UnreadableException` (an answer that is not what the spec says), `SocketClosedException`.
Callers `switch` over it exhaustively. Never classify by parsing a message. Argument mistakes
are `ArgumentError`, thrown before any I/O.

`RouterException` also carries the envelope `{"error": {"message", "type", "code", "doc_url"}}`
as `type` (a `RouterErrorType`, `unknown` for one newer than the SDK), `code` (an open string
to branch on), `docUrl` and `requestId` (the `X-Request-Id` header, what a 500 is quoted by),
and `retryAfterSeconds`, the `Retry-After` header as whole seconds (null for a date).

success schemas; any other body keeps its trimmed text (at most 1000 characters) or the
status phrase as the message, with the request id and the wait and nothing else. A refused socket
handshake stays a `TransportException`: `package:web_socket` gives a message only, no status,
headers or body.

## Public API

```dart
final agents = StreamAgents(url: url, customerId: 'acme');
final session = await agents.agent('support').sessions.create();
```

`ForkOptions`, `SessionQuery`, `SearchOptions`), not thirty named parameters.

Names chosen to not collide with what a Flutter app imports: `SearchRouter` (not `Router`),
`AgentImage` (not `ImageSource`), commands suffixed `Command`. Stream Chat also exports a
`Command`; a host importing both hides one.

asks again with its id and the `refresh_secret` stored beside it (`readGuest` and `writeGuest`

stored; one lost or spent gets a new guest. The store is the host's (shared preferences, secure storage);

## Views

and no `Scaffold`. A conversation is shown with Stream Chat's AI components, and

is kept working. What the router writes is what it renders:

  `AIMessage.reasoningText` reads it.

  showing the call `awaiting_approval` and calls `session.decideShown` with its step and the

  router holds itself (a connector's under `require_approval`, the agent's scheduling tools for a repeating task, #2533) never

  `AIVoiceGlowView` / `AIVoiceWaveView` show the agent on a call.

`call.state.valueStream`, `StreamVideoRenderer`, `call.getTrack(...).captureScreenshot()`.
Results are `Result<T>`; a `Failure` becomes `VoiceState.failure`.

  token expires an hour in.
- The camera starts on the back lens as a join setting, so no front-facing frame is published.
- The agent looks through the camera with the router's `get_video_frames` tool call, answered by
  `AgentSession` through `camera` and never offered to the app's tools. `camera` is a
  `CameraHandler`, `(at, limit)` to a list of `CameraPicture` records (both hidden from core's
  exports), and is public only because `rtc` is a separate area. It is `@internal` (`package:meta`), so the analyzer warns an
  app that touches it and its signature is `rtc`'s to change; `rtc`'s uses carry an `ignore`. With `camera` null the call is
  left alone (a backend video worker may own it); with `run: false` it is left alone too, as JS
  does; a `tool_cancel` drops the answer, as for the app's tools. Core reads `at_ms` and `limit`
  (1 to 8), sends the pictures oldest first as `camera-n`, and answers an empty list or a throw
  with the nothing-recent words.
- `VoiceSession` sets `camera` while its camera is on, and `stop`s and clears it on camera off
  (before Stream Video turns it off, so a look under way cannot finish on the pictures it took),
  `leave` and `end`. Stream Video 1.6 has no Dart hook on outgoing frames, so `CameraShots` takes
  a screenshot of the call's own track when the agent asks: `limit` pictures asked for 0.5 s apart, each
  the camera's next frame at full size (a JPEG on Android, a PNG on iOS), scaled to 1024 px and
  made JPEG q70 in `compute` (`package:image`, its JPEG and PNG decoders only, from 4.12.0, the first whose
  decoders do not throw on short data). Nothing is taken while idle and nothing kept, so
  `at` is not looked back to: the pictures come from just after the question, where iOS and
  Android send the ones from just before it. Matching them needs a native frame processor in
  `rtc` (`ProcessorProvider` and `setVideoEffects`); `camera` already carries `at` and each
  `capturedAt`, so that changes nothing public.
- A screenshot cannot be called off: its sink stays on the track until a frame comes. So a track
  that still owes a picture shares it rather than being asked again, even across the camera
  turned off and on. `stop` makes a look under way come back empty at once, even one waiting on
  a stalled track, since what a camera turned off showed is not for the agent. `captureFrame`
  writes every picture to the one `captureFrame.png` in the temp directory, so an app taking its
  own `takeScreenshot` at the same moment can swap pictures with it. Several full-size pictures pass the router's 5 MiB socket
  frame limit, which closes the socket; hence the scaling. A socket that names its `tools` must
  name `get_video_frames` too, or the router sends the call with `run: false` and drops the
  answer.
- Permissions are the host app's: `RECORD_AUDIO`, `MODIFY_AUDIO_SETTINGS`, `CAMERA`,
  `BLUETOOTH_CONNECT`, `INTERNET`, `ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE`; `NSMicrophoneUsageDescription`,
  `NSCameraUsageDescription`. Emulators do not test echo cancellation or audio routing.

## Tests

`package:test` in core and chat, `flutter_test` in rtc, all run by `flutter test`. Never mock; assert on state and outputs,
never on a call happening.

1. **The state machine**, on real frames, with no network.
2. **The client** against a real HTTP and WebSocket server on loopback (`test/support/router.dart`
   in core; rtc has its own small one), recording what arrived.
3. **Live tests**, tagged `live` and skipped unless `VISION_AGENTS_URL` is set: real sessions, a
   real model answer, a real tool call, rewind and fork, guests, search.
4. **The posture**: `posture_test.dart` drives every public operation against the loopback
   router and checks each request against `x-client-accessible` in the spec;
   `keyed_router_posture_test.dart` (tagged `live`, skipped without `INTEGRATION_ROUTER_KEY`)
   checks a real `api_key` router answers a device 403 `server_side_only`.
   `stream_clients_test.dart` covers the shared clients.

Wait on a condition with a deadline (`_until`), never a fixed sleep.

CI is [`client-sdks.yml`](../../../.github/workflows/client-sdks.yml), on any change under
`sdks/dart`, `flutter_demo`, `flutter_assistant` or the spec: one Flutter job with the checks and
tests below, then `flutter analyze` and `flutter test` in both examples against the package as
it is in the checkout.

Flutter 3.50 deprecates `package:flutter/material.dart`. Each import of it carries
`// ignore: deprecated_member_use` rather than a global ignore, so any other deprecation still
fails the analyzer.

Docker only, pub's cache in the named volume `va-dart-pub`:

```bash
docker run --rm -v "$PWD":/repo -v va-dart-pub:/pub-cache -e PUB_CACHE=/pub-cache \
  -w /repo/sdks/dart/stream_agents ghcr.io/cirruslabs/flutter:3.44.0 \
  sh -c 'flutter pub get && dart format --set-exit-if-changed . && flutter analyze && dart run tool/generate.dart --check && flutter test'
# live, against a router on the host
docker run --rm -v "$PWD":/repo -v va-dart-pub:/pub-cache -e PUB_CACHE=/pub-cache \
  -e VISION_AGENTS_URL=http://host.docker.internal:8080 -e VISION_AGENTS_CUSTOMER_ID=examples \
  -e VISION_AGENTS_AGENT=simple_voice_ai -w /repo/sdks/dart/stream_agents ghcr.io/cirruslabs/flutter:3.44.0 flutter test -t live
```

## Releasing

`.github/workflows/release-sdk-dart.yml` publishes the version `pubspec.yaml` names, by hand or
with every other SDK (see the `release-sdks` skill); by hand it is `flutter pub publish` from
`sdks/dart/stream_agents`, after the CI dry run passes. A release
sets `sdkVersion` in `lib/src/core/backend.dart` with the `version` in `pubspec.yaml`, since a
package cannot read its own pubspec when it runs: it is the release `X-Stream-Client` and
`User-Agent` name, and a test fails until the two match. A browser sends no `User-Agent` of
the SDK's (`userAgent` is null there), since neither CORS list allows it. The first
release of `stream_agents` also discontinues `stream_agents_core`, `stream_agents_chat` and
`stream_agents_rtc` on pub.dev, each with `stream_agents` as its replacement (the package's
admin page, "Mark as discontinued"), so an app on 0.1.0 is pointed at the one package.

## Reviewing a change

Reject it if it:

- imports Flutter, `dart:io` or a Stream package into `lib/src/core`, or crosses areas other
  than through `core`'s barrel;
- exports generated code, or hand-edits it;
- adds a method for an operation the spec does not mark `x-client-accessible`;
- sends a default the caller did not choose;
- reconnects the socket, or replays `respond`/`tool_result`;
- treats an unknown frame as fatal;
- uses the `StreamVideo` singleton factory;
- adds conversation views to the SDK rather than to Stream Chat's AI components;
- adds a theme object, a route push or a `Scaffold` to `rtc`;
- mocks, or asserts that a method was called.

`Command`; a host importing both hides one.

Guests: `guestUser` reuses what the `GuestStore` holds until a minute before it expires, then
asks again with its id and the `refresh_secret` stored beside it (`readGuest` and `writeGuest`
keep it off the public `GuestUser`). A secret works once, so whatever comes back replaces what was
stored; one lost or spent gets a new guest. The store is the host's (shared preferences, secure storage);
`MemoryGuestStore` is for tests and CLIs.

## Views

`rtc` has the only widgets, `AgentVideoView` and `VoiceCallView`: no theme object, no route push
and no `Scaffold`. A conversation is shown with Stream Chat's AI components, and
[`flutter_demo`](../../../examples/voice_agents/flutter_demo) is where that composition lives and
is kept working. What the router writes is what it renders:

- A text session's reply is a message marked `ai_generated`, with `generating` true until done.
- Its steps are `ai_reasoning` and `ai_tool_call` attachments, in order: `AIMessagePart.parseAll`
  over `(type: attachment.rawType, payload: {'id': attachment.id, ...attachment.extraData})`.
- A reasoning step stores only its opening. The whole of it comes a window at a time on the
  `message.updated` events; `LiveReasoning` in `chat` puts it back together, and the demo's
  `AIMessage.reasoningText` reads it.
- A tool that asks first is answered by an `AIToolApprover` whose `decide` finds the reply
  showing the call `awaiting_approval` and calls `session.decideShown` with its step and the
  reply's `support_runtime` (`command_id`, `turn_id`), or `session.decide` for a call only the
  session holds; on a call, by an `AIToolApprovalCard` over `session.approvals`. A call the
  router holds itself (a connector's under `require_approval`, the agent's scheduling tools for a repeating task, #2533) never
  reaches `approvals`, so only `decideShown` answers it.
- `AIConversationView` lays the channel out in turns, `ChatComposer` asks and stops, and
  `AIVoiceGlowView` / `AIVoiceWaveView` show the agent on a call.

## rtc

The Stream Video 1.6 surface used: `StreamVideo.create(apiKey, user: User.regular(...),
userToken:, tokenLoader:)`, `makeCall(callType:, id:)`, `call.join(connectOptions:
CallConnectOptions(microphone:, camera:, cameraFacingMode: FacingMode.environment,
speakerDefaultOn: true))` (which creates the call too), `setMicrophoneEnabled`,
`setCameraEnabled(constraints: CameraConstraints(...))`, `call.leave()`, `dispose()`,
`call.state.valueStream`, `StreamVideoRenderer`, `call.getTrack(...).captureScreenshot()`.
Results are `Result<T>`; a `Failure` becomes `VoiceState.failure`.

- A token provider, not a token: `tokenLoader` asks the agents' token function again when the
  token expires an hour in.
- The camera starts on the back lens as a join setting, so no front-facing frame is published.
- The agent looks through the camera with the router's `get_video_frames` tool call, answered by
  `AgentSession` through `camera` and never offered to the app's tools. `camera` is a
  `CameraHandler`, `(at, limit)` to a list of `CameraPicture` records (both hidden from core's
  exports), and is public only because `rtc` is a separate area. It is `@internal` (`package:meta`), so the analyzer warns an
  app that touches it and its signature is `rtc`'s to change; `rtc`'s uses carry an `ignore`. With `camera` null the call is
  left alone (a backend video worker may own it); with `run: false` it is left alone too, as JS
  does; a `tool_cancel` drops the answer, as for the app's tools. Core reads `at_ms` and `limit`
  (1 to 8), sends the pictures oldest first as `camera-n`, and answers an empty list or a throw
  with the nothing-recent words.
- `VoiceSession` sets `camera` while its camera is on, and `stop`s and clears it on camera off
  (before Stream Video turns it off, so a look under way cannot finish on the pictures it took),
  `leave` and `end`. Stream Video 1.6 has no Dart hook on outgoing frames, so `CameraShots` takes
  a screenshot of the call's own track when the agent asks: `limit` pictures asked for 0.5 s apart, each
  the camera's next frame at full size (a JPEG on Android, a PNG on iOS), scaled to 1024 px and
  made JPEG q70 in `compute` (`package:image`, its JPEG and PNG decoders only, from 4.12.0, the first whose
  decoders do not throw on short data). Nothing is taken while idle and nothing kept, so
  `at` is not looked back to: the pictures come from just after the question, where iOS and
  Android send the ones from just before it. Matching them needs a native frame processor in
  `rtc` (`ProcessorProvider` and `setVideoEffects`); `camera` already carries `at` and each
  `capturedAt`, so that changes nothing public.
- A screenshot cannot be called off: its sink stays on the track until a frame comes. So a track
  that still owes a picture shares it rather than being asked again, even across the camera
  turned off and on. `stop` makes a look under way come back empty at once, even one waiting on
  a stalled track, since what a camera turned off showed is not for the agent. `captureFrame`
  writes every picture to the one `captureFrame.png` in the temp directory, so an app taking its
  own `takeScreenshot` at the same moment can swap pictures with it. Several full-size pictures pass the router's 5 MiB socket
  frame limit, which closes the socket; hence the scaling. A socket that names its `tools` must
  name `get_video_frames` too, or the router sends the call with `run: false` and drops the
  answer.
- Permissions are the host app's: `RECORD_AUDIO`, `MODIFY_AUDIO_SETTINGS`, `CAMERA`,
  `BLUETOOTH_CONNECT`, `INTERNET`, `ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE`; `NSMicrophoneUsageDescription`,
  `NSCameraUsageDescription`. Emulators do not test echo cancellation or audio routing.

## Tests

`package:test` in core and chat, `flutter_test` in rtc, all run by `flutter test`. Never mock; assert on state and outputs,
never on a call happening.

1. **The state machine**, on real frames, with no network.
2. **The client** against a real HTTP and WebSocket server on loopback (`test/support/router.dart`
   in core; rtc has its own small one), recording what arrived.
3. **Live tests**, tagged `live` and skipped unless `VISION_AGENTS_URL` is set: real sessions, a
   real model answer, a real tool call, rewind and fork, guests, search.
4. **The posture**: `posture_test.dart` drives every public operation against the loopback
   router and checks each request against `x-client-accessible` in the spec;
   `keyed_router_posture_test.dart` (tagged `live`, skipped without `INTEGRATION_ROUTER_KEY`)
   checks a real `api_key` router answers a device 403 `server_side_only`.
   `stream_clients_test.dart` covers the shared clients.

Wait on a condition with a deadline (`_until`), never a fixed sleep.

CI is [`client-sdks.yml`](../../../.github/workflows/client-sdks.yml), on any change under
`sdks/dart`, `flutter_demo`, `flutter_assistant` or the spec: one Flutter job with the checks and
tests below, then `flutter analyze` and `flutter test` in both examples against the package as
it is in the checkout.

Flutter 3.50 deprecates `package:flutter/material.dart`. Each import of it carries
`// ignore: deprecated_member_use` rather than a global ignore, so any other deprecation still
fails the analyzer.

Docker only, pub's cache in the named volume `va-dart-pub`:

```bash
docker run --rm -v "$PWD":/repo -v va-dart-pub:/pub-cache -e PUB_CACHE=/pub-cache \
  -w /repo/sdks/dart/stream_agents ghcr.io/cirruslabs/flutter:3.44.0 \
  sh -c 'flutter pub get && dart format --set-exit-if-changed . && flutter analyze && dart run tool/generate.dart --check && flutter test'
# live, against a router on the host
docker run --rm -v "$PWD":/repo -v va-dart-pub:/pub-cache -e PUB_CACHE=/pub-cache \
  -e VISION_AGENTS_URL=http://host.docker.internal:8080 -e VISION_AGENTS_CUSTOMER_ID=examples \
  -e VISION_AGENTS_AGENT=simple_voice_ai -w /repo/sdks/dart/stream_agents ghcr.io/cirruslabs/flutter:3.44.0 flutter test -t live
```

## Releasing

`.github/workflows/release-sdk-dart.yml` publishes the version `pubspec.yaml` names, by hand or
with every other SDK (see the `release-sdks` skill); by hand it is `flutter pub publish` from
`sdks/dart/stream_agents`, after the CI dry run passes. A release
sets `sdkVersion` in `lib/src/core/backend.dart` with the `version` in `pubspec.yaml`, since a
package cannot read its own pubspec when it runs: it is the release `X-Stream-Client` and
`User-Agent` name, and a test fails until the two match. A browser sends no `User-Agent` of
the SDK's (`userAgent` is null there), since neither CORS list allows it. The first
release of `stream_agents` also discontinues `stream_agents_core`, `stream_agents_chat` and
`stream_agents_rtc` on pub.dev, each with `stream_agents` as its replacement (the package's
admin page, "Mark as discontinued"), so an app on 0.1.0 is pointed at the one package.

## Reviewing a change

Reject it if it:

- imports Flutter, `dart:io` or a Stream package into `lib/src/core`, or crosses areas other
  than through `core`'s barrel;
- exports generated code, or hand-edits it;
- adds a method for an operation the spec does not mark `x-client-accessible`;
- sends a default the caller did not choose;
- reconnects the socket, or replays `respond`/`tool_result`;
- treats an unknown frame as fatal;
- uses the `StreamVideo` singleton factory;
- adds conversation views to the SDK rather than to Stream Chat's AI components;
- adds a theme object, a route push or a `Scaffold` to `rtc`;
- mocks, or asserts that a method was called.

---
name: sdk-dotnet
description: How to build and extend the .NET SDK in sdks/dotnet. Read this before changing the client, the socket, the agent, dispatch or the router, before regenerating the models, or before reaching for a NuGet package.
---

# .NET SDK conventions

The per-language half of [sdk](../sdk/SKILL.md). It records the decisions
[`sdks/dotnet`](../../../sdks/dotnet) already follows, so a change lands consistently rather
than re-litigating them.

Assume .NET 10 (the LTS), C# 14, `net10.0`, nullable reference types on, warnings as errors,
central package management (`Directory.Packages.props`). Server side only.

## Toolchain: Docker, never the host

Nothing is installed on the host. Every command runs in `mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:10.0`
with the repo mounted and the NuGet cache in the `va-nuget` volume:

```bash
D="docker run --rm -v /path/to/Vision-Agents:/repo -v va-nuget:/root/.nuget -w /repo/sdks/dotnet mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:10.0"
$D dotnet build GetStream.VisionAgents.slnx
$D dotnet test --project tests/GetStream.VisionAgents.Tests
$D dotnet run --project tools/Generate              # regenerate the models
$D dotnet run --project tools/Generate -- --check   # what CI runs
docker run ... -e VISION_AGENTS_LIVE_URL=http://host.docker.internal:8091 ... \
  dotnet test --project tests/GetStream.VisionAgents.Tests -- --filter-class GetStream.VisionAgents.Tests.LiveTests
```

Build output (`bin/`, `obj/`, `TestResults/`) is ignored by `sdks/dotnet/.gitignore`, nowhere
else.

## Naming

Stream's .NET packages are `getstream-net` (the current generated server SDK, namespace
`GetStream`), `stream-chat-net` and `stream-feed-net`. The package id is the placeholder
**`getstream-calypso`**, like the JS `@stream-io/calypso`, until the public name is chosen; the
namespace stays **`GetStream.VisionAgents`**, with the generated DTOs under
`GetStream.VisionAgents.Models`.

Releases run by hand: Actions, "Release .NET SDK", "Use workflow from" `main`, pick the
part to bump or type an exact version, and untick the dry run to publish. The workflow is
`.github/workflows/release-sdk-dotnet.yml`; it pushes to NuGet through trusted publishing and
tags `sdk-dotnet-v<version>`. Keep the file name: the nuget.org policy is bound to it. Do not rename to `StreamIO.*`; nothing
Stream ships to NuGet is called that.

Public types are named after what they are to a caller (`Agent`, `Session`, `Dispatch`,
`Router`, `Folder`), async methods end in `Async` and take a `CancellationToken` last,
defaulted. Options are `sealed record`s with `init` properties.

## The generator: NSwag, DTOs only

`tools/Generate` uses NSwag 14.7.1 **as a library**, writing
`src/GetStream.VisionAgents/Generated/Models.cs`. The output is committed, so a restore needs no
code generation, and `--check` fails CI when the spec has moved without it.

Why NSwag, and why DTOs only:

- **The request layer has to be ours.** A token is minted per request, a local router takes
  `X-Customer-Id`, a hosted one wants `api_key` and `stream-auth-type`, and sockets carry the
  same credential. A generated client brings a runtime that decides those things, and it
  decides them differently. So the generator emits POCOs and `VisionAgentsClient` has one
  method per HTTP verb (`GetAsync<T>`, `PostAsync<T>`, ...), the way sdk-js does.
- **Kiota** was the other serious option. It generates request builders over its own
  abstractions (`Microsoft.Kiota.*` packages at runtime), its models are not plain
  `System.Text.Json` types, and it cannot be told to emit models alone. That is a runtime
  dependency and an auth pipeline to fight for types we only need the shapes of.
- **openapi-generator** needs a JVM, emits an `ApiClient`/`Configuration` runtime, and its
  `System.Text.Json` path is the less-travelled one.
- **Refitter** generates Refit interfaces, so Refit at runtime, for the same reason no.
- NSwag emits `System.Text.Json` POCOs with nullable reference types, runs on the same .NET
  image, and is pinned in `Directory.Packages.props`. The library rather than the CLI because
  the CLI cannot be told two things that make the output usable: PascalCase property names
  (`PascalCaseNames`) and enums as strings (`EnumsAsStrings`). A C# enum has nowhere to put a
  value the router adds after this ships, so an enum would fail the whole response; the
  values stay in the doc comment.
- `GenerateDefaultValues = false` and optional properties nullable: **never copy a schema
  default into a request.** A default sent because the type had one is how a caller silently
  loses what their config named. A field left null is left out, so the config or the router
  decides.

Never hand-edit `Generated/Models.cs`. Never re-declare a schema by hand; use the model.

## Dependencies

- **getstream-net 16.0.1** for what is Stream rather than this router: `Edge` mints user
  tokens (`CreateUserToken`) and can still create a call (`VideoClient.GetOrCreateCallAsync`),
  though agents no longer need one created: the router names it after the session. It refuses a
  secret shorter than 256 bits, which a real Stream secret never is; test fixtures use a
  64-character one. Its exceptions are wrapped in `RouterException`.
- **YamlDotNet 18.1.0** for `agent.yaml`, `urls.yaml` and skill frontmatter, with duplicate
  keys refused. A key `agent.yaml` does not know is refused, not dropped.
- Tokens for the router itself are HS256 signed with `System.Security.Cryptography`, not a JWT
  package: a dozen lines in `Backend.SignToken`.
- Nothing else at runtime. A new package is a design question; ask first.

## HttpClient

`new VisionAgentsClient(options)` owns its `HttpClient`; `new VisionAgentsClient(httpClient,
options)` borrows one, which is how `IHttpClientFactory` plugs in, and never disposes it.
`Agent` disposes a client only if it made it. Do not add a DI extension package.

## Errors

Every answer that is not a success becomes a `RouterException` in one place,
`RouterException.Answered`, which reads the generated `ErrorResponse`: `Said` is its message,
`Type` (a string, so a kind the router adds later still reads) and `Code` are what to branch on,
`DocUrl` explains the code, and `RequestId` is the `X-Request-Id` to quote when a 500 says only
"something went wrong". A body that is not the envelope (a proxy's page, nothing, an older
router's `{"error": "..."}`) keeps its trimmed text as `Said` with the rest null, and a refused
socket upgrade has no body at all, because `ClientWebSocket` keeps only the status and headers.

## Sockets

Hand-written in `Socket.cs`, because OpenAPI stops at the upgrade. One `Socket` over
`ClientWebSocket` for the session events, dispatch and the modality streams.

- Server side, so **credentials go in headers**, never the query string.
- Frames are loose (`Frame`, read through `Text`, `Flag`, `Number`, `Nested`), so a frame type
  the router learns later reaches a caller rather than being dropped.
- The modality start frame carries `target` at the top level as well as inside the option
  block, like Go and the Python plugin: the router refuses a frame whose target is only in the
  block (see `readStart` in `acceleration/internal/api/streamws.go`), although the spec
  describes only the block.
- No automatic reconnection on session sockets: `respond` and `tool_result` are not
  idempotent. `Dispatch` redials its own socket (see below).

## Sessions and tools

- The watch loop starts when the session opens and handles `tool_call` and `tool_cancel`
  itself, so a tool runs whether or not anybody iterates `EventsAsync`. At most 16 run at
  once; a tool that throws is answered with its message, because the model is mid-sentence
  waiting.
- `EventsAsync` has one reader over a bounded 256-slot channel that drops the oldest.
- `CloseAsync` sends `close` over an open socket, else DELETEs the session; a 404 is fine.
- Rewinding a conversation kept in Stream Chat is refused by the router (400, "fork it at the
  response"); `ForkAsync(new ForkOptions { ResponseId = ... })` is the way.

## Agent and folder

- Sessions own their call, `agent:<session id>`. `JoinAsync` opens one with `start_voice`;
  `JoinAsync(InboundCall)` opens the session the call names, with voice; `ChatAsync` sends no
  `start_voice`; `Session.Voice` starts and stops it later. `OutboundCallAsync` places the call
  first, then joins the session it returns with `navigating`; `WaitForCallAsync` attaches the
  number, waits on a one-call `Dispatch` for the router to hand a call over, joins it and
  returns once somebody speaks. `ResumeAsync(id)` reads a session and watches it.
- Instructions reach the backend only through `SyncAsync`; nothing sends them per session.
- `Config` is a directory holding `agent.yaml` or a stored config's name; `ConfigId` is a
  stored config by id, which is what a dispatched message carries. Naming both is refused.
- What code sets wins over what the directory says.
- `SyncAsync` is one `POST /v1/agents/sync`. The fingerprint is **MD5, ported byte for byte
  from Go** (`Folder.Fingerprint`, `Folder.GoMap` for Go's `%v` of a map), so `.agent_sync`
  written by Go or Python is read back here. The fixture hash `02a7b2c8428f31e3a2b93ca2f5a6ec70`
  is pinned in `FolderTests`; if it changes, Go changed first or this is wrong. The stamp is
  written with relaxed escaping, since `System.Text.Json` would otherwise write the `+` of the
  offset as `\u002B`.

## Dispatch

- Handlers run off the read loop in `Task.Run`, tracked by id in a `ConcurrentDictionary`
  whose entry is removed before the tracking task completes, so `Active` is exact once
  `RunAsync` has drained.
- `RunAsync` returns quietly when cancelled, even during connect, then drains work in flight
  and closes the agents it made. Dropping work would hang up on whoever is talking.
- `GetOrCreateAgentAsync` keeps one agent per channel while its session is live, and opens
  chats with the message's `AgentId`, as Go and Python do.
- `Host(client, toolTimeout)` sends `host_tools` for `client.Tools` with `every_agent: true` after every `ready`; `client.RunDispatchAsync()` hosts them alone. Hosted calls are
  tracked work like calls, and `hosting_refused` throws out of `RunAsync`. A connection
  that ends without a normal close is redialled with backoff (1s doubling to 30s), as in
  Go. This is the one socket that reconnects: dispatch frames belong to one connection.

## Tests

xUnit v3 (4.0.1) on the Microsoft Testing Platform (`global.json` sets the runner), because
.NET 10's `dotnet test` no longer drives VSTest here. Never mock.

- `TestRouter` is a real Kestrel server on loopback port 0 with real WebSocket upgrades. It
  records what arrived and lets a test script frames. Assert on what reached the far end.
- Getstream-net is pointed at the same server through `EdgeOptions.BaseUrl`, so a test can
  assert that no Stream call is created.
- `LiveTests` skip unless `VISION_AGENTS_LIVE_URL` is set. They hold real conversations and
  wait for what the router writes behind a request instead of sleeping.

`ClientWebSocket` for the session events, dispatch and the modality streams.

- Server side, so **credentials go in headers**, never the query string.
- Frames are loose (`Frame`, read through `Text`, `Flag`, `Number`, `Nested`), so a frame type
  the router learns later reaches a caller rather than being dropped.
- The modality start frame carries `target` at the top level as well as inside the option
  block, like Go and the Python plugin: the router refuses a frame whose target is only in the
  block (see `readStart` in `acceleration/internal/api/streamws.go`), although the spec
  describes only the block.
- No automatic reconnection on session sockets: `respond` and `tool_result` are not
  idempotent. `Dispatch` redials its own socket (see below).

## Sessions and tools

- The watch loop starts when the session opens and handles `tool_call` and `tool_cancel`
  itself, so a tool runs whether or not anybody iterates `EventsAsync`. At most 16 run at
  once; a tool that throws is answered with its message, because the model is mid-sentence
  waiting.
- `EventsAsync` has one reader over a bounded 256-slot channel that drops the oldest.
- `CloseAsync` sends `close` over an open socket, else DELETEs the session; a 404 is fine.
- Rewinding a conversation kept in Stream Chat is refused by the router (400, "fork it at the
  response"); `ForkAsync(new ForkOptions { ResponseId = ... })` is the way.

## Agent and folder

- Sessions own their call, `agent:<session id>`. `JoinAsync` opens one with `start_voice`;
  `JoinAsync(InboundCall)` opens the session the call names, with voice; `ChatAsync` sends no
  `start_voice`; `Session.Voice` starts and stops it later. `OutboundCallAsync` places the call
  first, then joins the session it returns with `navigating`; `WaitForCallAsync` attaches the
  number, waits on a one-call `Dispatch` for the router to hand a call over, joins it and
  returns once somebody speaks. `ResumeAsync(id)` reads a session and watches it.
- Instructions reach the backend only through `SyncAsync`; nothing sends them per session.
- `Config` is a directory holding `agent.yaml` or a stored config's name; `ConfigId` is a
  stored config by id, which is what a dispatched message carries. Naming both is refused.
- What code sets wins over what the directory says.
- `SyncAsync` is one `POST /v1/agents/sync`. The fingerprint is **MD5, ported byte for byte
  from Go** (`Folder.Fingerprint`, `Folder.GoMap` for Go's `%v` of a map), so `.agent_sync`
  written by Go or Python is read back here. The fixture hash `02a7b2c8428f31e3a2b93ca2f5a6ec70`
  is pinned in `FolderTests`; if it changes, Go changed first or this is wrong. The stamp is
  written with relaxed escaping, since `System.Text.Json` would otherwise write the `+` of the
  offset as `\u002B`.

## Dispatch

- Handlers run off the read loop in `Task.Run`, tracked by id in a `ConcurrentDictionary`
  whose entry is removed before the tracking task completes, so `Active` is exact once
  `RunAsync` has drained.
- `RunAsync` returns quietly when cancelled, even during connect, then drains work in flight
  and closes the agents it made. Dropping work would hang up on whoever is talking.
- `GetOrCreateAgentAsync` keeps one agent per channel while its session is live, and opens
  chats with the message's `AgentId`, as Go and Python do.
- `Host(client, toolTimeout)` sends `host_tools` for `client.Tools` with `every_agent: true` after every `ready`; `client.RunDispatchAsync()` hosts them alone. Hosted calls are
  tracked work like calls, and `hosting_refused` throws out of `RunAsync`. A connection
  that ends without a normal close is redialled with backoff (1s doubling to 30s), as in
  Go. This is the one socket that reconnects: dispatch frames belong to one connection.

## Tests

xUnit v3 (4.0.1) on the Microsoft Testing Platform (`global.json` sets the runner), because
.NET 10's `dotnet test` no longer drives VSTest here. Never mock.

- `TestRouter` is a real Kestrel server on loopback port 0 with real WebSocket upgrades. It
  records what arrived and lets a test script frames. Assert on what reached the far end.
- Getstream-net is pointed at the same server through `EdgeOptions.BaseUrl`, so a test can
  assert that no Stream call is created.
- `LiveTests` skip unless `VISION_AGENTS_LIVE_URL` is set. They hold real conversations and
  wait for what the router writes behind a request instead of sleeping.

---
name: sdk-go
description: How the Go SDK in sdks/go is built, tested and released. Read before changing sdks/go, adding a resource method, or cutting a Go SDK version.
---

# Go SDK conventions

The per-language half of [sdk](../sdk/SKILL.md) for [`sdks/go`](../../../sdks/go), module
`github.com/GetStream/Vision-Agents/sdks/go`. Go goes first (AGENTS.md "SDK changes"), so a
shared API change lands here before the other SDKs. Write the Go itself by the
[go](../go/SKILL.md) and [go-testing](../go-testing/SKILL.md) skills.

## Layout

| Package | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `agents` | An agent spelled out in code: `agents.New`, folder sync, tools, phone, dispatch workers (`agents.NewDispatch`). What most programs start from |
| `client` | Agents addressed by name (`client.New(backend).Agent("docs")`), their sessions, responses, items, forks, guests, usage callbacks |
| `stream` | `Backend` (where the router is, who is billed), `Pipeline` (one session and its socket), `RouterError`, routers (`stream.NewClient(backend).Router(name)`), phone |
| `tools` | The function registry and the JSON Schema read off an argument struct |
| `edge` | Stream Video calls and the monitor link, through `getstream-go` |
| `acceleration` | Generated from the spec. Never edited by hand |

`stream.Backend` is the one value every package shares. A client's `Backend()` carries its
usage watcher, so an agent, worker or router built on it reports to that client's
`WithUsage` and `WithBalanceWarning`; `client.New` with no options on such a backend shares
the watcher rather than wrapping it twice.

## Go version

Always keep the SDK to latest version of Golang

## Dependencies

- Always update dependencies to latest version
- Changes to dependencies cannot break the public API

## The generated client

`go generate ./...` in `sdks/go` runs oapi-codegen on `../../acceleration/api/openapi.yaml` with
`api/oapi-codegen.yaml`, which leaves out the `Staff` operations and the four socket
operations: `stream` holds the three it uses by hand on `stream/socket.go`, and
`openSocketSession` has no Go client yet. The output is committed; CI's `go` job regenerates
it and fails on a diff.

Models public, operations not:

- Generated types (`acceleration.Session`, `AgentConfig`, `SttOptions`, enums) are the SDK's
  models and may appear in signatures. Do not wrap one for its own sake.
- Generated operations (`*WithResponse`) are never the API: README, examples and docs call a
  method of `client`, `agents` or `stream`. A new endpoint is finished when it has one.
- `stream.Backend.Client()` and `agents.Agent.Client()` hand out the generated client for an
  operation with no method yet. Their doc comments say it carries no compatibility promise;
  keep that true and add no third accessor.
- A parameter never takes `*acceleration.ClientWithResponses`. Take a `stream.Backend`.

Known gaps, generated only (docs on getstream.io call some of them raw today): simulations and
their runs, voices, knowledge documents and URLs beyond ingest and add, scheduled tasks,
campaigns, channels, connectors, a connection's credentials and tools, SIP trunks, 10DLC and opt-outs, phone
transfer, digits and release, account, credits, spend limits, usage events, teams, prices,
stats, policies, provider keys, runs, OCR and classify. Folder sync does not read
`resume_history:` from agent.yaml yet, so one that names it is refused.

## Errors, retries and idempotency

- Every refusal is a `*stream.RouterError`, built by `stream.NewRouterError` from the answer.
  Transport failures are wrapped with `%w`, so `errors.Is(err, context.Canceled)` holds.
- The SDK retries no HTTP request: it cannot know which of the caller's are safe to send twice.
  `RouterError.RetryAfter` says how long the router asked for.
- `Responses.Create` sends a fresh `request_id` per text question, so the router answers a
  resend once. A tool call is keyed by its id (`tools.Registry` receipts), so a call the router
  sends again is joined or answered from its first result.
- A text session's socket is the one thing reconnected: doubling waits from one second to 30,
  for five minutes (`Pipeline.firstRetry`, `resumeFor`), giving up on a 4xx other than 429.

## Tests

```bash
cd sdks/go
go test -race ./...
go vet ./... && go vet -tags e2e .
```

No mocks: each package has its own stand-in router, an `httptest.Server` with a real gorilla
upgrader (`router` in `client/client_test.go` and `stream/accelerated_test.go`, `restartable`
and `reopened` in `stream/resume_test.go`, `pool` in `stream/dispatch_test.go`, `worked` in
`agents/dispatch_test.go`, `backend` in `agents/agent_test.go`, `moneyRouter` in
`client/usage_test.go`, `vendors` in `stream/phone_test.go`). Reuse the package's own before
writing another. `readme_test.go` holds the README's quickstart to `examples/quickstart`.

`e2e_test.go` (tag `e2e`) drives a real router and real models, so it costs money and never
runs in CI. Without `STREAM_ACCELERATION_URL` it skips; with `E2E_REQUIRED=1` every skip fails
instead. Its package comment names the release smoke set; run it against a router that
searches, holds knowledge and bills:

```bash
E2E_REQUIRED=1 go test -tags e2e -count=1 -v -run "$SMOKE" .
```

## README

The README renders on pkg.go.dev too, where only links inside the module resolve: a link
outside `sdks/go` is an absolute `https://github.com/GetStream/Vision-Agents/tree/main/...`.
Every identifier in a code block exists; the quickstart is the example file verbatim.

## Releasing

`sdks/go` is developed and released on `main`, the default branch, so `go get ...@latest`,
`@main` and pkg.go.dev see it. A version is a tag `sdks/go/vX.Y.Z` on a `main` commit; nothing
is copied. While 0.x, a minor may break a signature; a patch only fixes.

1. Land the change on `main` by a pull request, with `Version` in `stream/backend.go` set to
   `X.Y.Z`: it is the `User-Agent` every request sends (`stream-agents-go/X.Y.Z`) and its
   `X-Stream-Client` (`stream-agents-go-vX.Y.Z`), and nothing else sets it. `release-sdk-go.yml` fails a tag whose `Version` differs. If the change breaks a
   signature or field, add one line under `# Unreleased` → **Breaking Changes** in the root
   `CHANGELOG.md`. The `Go SDK` steps of the `CI (SDKs)` workflow (`.github/workflows/ci-sdks.yml`)
   check `sdks/go` alone on Go 1.25, as a consumer gets it.
2. Check out the commit to tag (`git switch --detach <the main commit>`), run the smoke set
   from `sdks/go` with `E2E_REQUIRED=1`, as above, and keep its output, so the result is the
   tagged commit's.
3. Tag the commit that holds the change by its SHA, not whatever `main` is by then. Never
   create a GitHub Release for it: `release.yml` publishes the Python packages on a release.
   Check its `Version` first, as below: the proxy takes a pushed tag before the workflow runs,
   so a tag the workflow refuses stays public (`v0.5.0` did).

   ```bash
   set -euo pipefail   # a failed check below stops before the tag
   git fetch origin
   SHA=<the main commit>
   git merge-base --is-ancestor "$SHA" origin/main   # exits 0, else the script stops
   git show "$SHA:sdks/go/stream/backend.go" | grep -q 'Version = "X.Y.Z"'   # the workflow's own check
   git tag sdks/go/vX.Y.Z "$SHA"
   git push origin sdks/go/vX.Y.Z
   ```

4. `release-sdk-go.yml` runs on the tag: it checks the tag is on `main`, checks the tagged copy
   and builds the quickstart in an empty module through proxy.golang.org. By hand, with
   `GOPRIVATE` cleared:

   ```bash
   GOPRIVATE= GONOSUMDB= GOFLAGS=-mod=mod GOPROXY=https://proxy.golang.org \
     go list -m -versions github.com/GetStream/Vision-Agents/sdks/go
   ```

A version found broken is never moved or deleted: the proxy and the checksum database keep it.
Add `retract vX.Y.Z // why` to `sdks/go/go.mod` on `main`, and release the next patch the
same way; `@latest` then skips the retracted one.

## Reject in review

- A `*WithResponse` call in the README, an example or a docs page where a method exists.
- A parameter of a generated client type, or a new accessor for the generated client.
- A retry of an HTTP request without an owner, a bound and a named threat (AGENTS.md).
- A stdlib or language feature newer than the `go` directive.
